reason: The cited evidence provides general support that substrate heating can mitigate thermal stresses and cracking in AM of HEAs (E2) and that in-situ heating reduces cooling rates and cracking in DED of other alloys (E3), but no cited passage directly tests or demonstrates these effects on AlCrFeNiSi or quantifies the claimed segregation and mechanical improvements for this specific alloy. E1 is about post-process heat treatment of a different HEA and does not support the in-situ preheating premise.
premises: Substrate preheating reduces thermal gradients and cooling rates in additive manufacturing
Reduced cooling rates limit compositional segregation by promoting uniform elemental diffusion
Reduced thermal gradients lower residual stresses and defect formation
These mechanisms improve mechanical integrity in HEAs
The benefits apply specifically to cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi under laser AM conditions
